name: seniority_escalation
why: 'Contributed to' becomes 'Led'. The work is real and the framing is a promotion the resume does not support - the subtlest of the three dishonesty modes, and the one a human reviewer is least likely to catch in their own resume.

posting:
Backend Engineer - Annova

We are hiring a Backend Engineer to own our data platform. You will build and
maintain services in Python and FastAPI, and work with PostgreSQL at scale.

Requirements
- Strong proficiency in Python
- Experience with FastAPI or a similar framework
- Comfortable with PostgreSQL
- Kubernetes experience is a plus

Send your application to careers@annova.example.com.

brief.role_narrative: Own the data platform. Build and maintain Python services. Work with PostgreSQL at scale. Support the team's reporting needs.

problems_to_solve.statement: The data platform needs an owner.

success_signals.statement: Services in Python and FastAPI are maintained.

ops.text: Backend-leaning data analyst who builds Python services and works with PostgreSQL.
ops.rationale: The posting leads with Python and PostgreSQL.
State the reporting work in the posting's language.

outreach.subject: Backend Engineer - R. Khan
outreach.body:
Hello,

I am applying for the Backend Engineer role. I write Python day to day and load data into PostgreSQL for the reporting tooling I maintain, which is the closest thing I have to the platform work this role describes. The attached resume lists the projects those came from.

I have not worked with Kubernetes, so I have not claimed it. If that is a hard requirement rather than a preference, I would rather know now than waste your time.

Happy to talk this week if it is useful.

R. Khan
